messages.content: Write the answer as Markdown prose. Return only the text of the answer, with no preface and no closing remarks.

You write one exchange of dialogue in a fiction story: a short scene in which two or more characters speak, each in their own voice.

Core idea: Two keepers can disagree and still share the same light.
Goal: Agree whether to send a signal to the mainland.
Scene: Night. The supply boat is three weeks late. The two keepers sit at the table with the logbook open between them.
Subtext: Each of them is afraid of being the first to say the boat will not come.
Length: 600 words.
Tone: spare.
Characters:
character nell-carrow (entities/nell-carrow.md)
---
type: character
name: Nell Carrow
want: To keep the light lit without help.
need: To accept that the light is shared.
flaw: Pride in doing everything alone.
voice: Terse. Short sentences, no greetings, numbers before names.
relationships:
  - character: pim-dorey
    note: Her relief keeper. She tolerates his talk and does not answer it.
---

Nell Carrow has kept the light for nineteen winters.
character pim-dorey (entities/pim-dorey.md)
---
type: character
name: Pim Dorey
want: To be trusted with the light.
need: To stop filling silences.
flaw: Talks when afraid.
voice: Talkative. Long run-on sentences, questions, first names for everyone.
relationships:
  - character: nell-carrow
    note: His senior keeper. He wants her approval and fills the silence she leaves.
---

Pim Dorey arrived on the last supply boat and has not stopped talking since.
Material:
place skerry-light (entities/skerry-light.md)
Skerry Light is a lamp on a bare rock, reached only on a spring tide.
style-profile plain-spoken (entities/plain-spoken.md)
---
type: style-profile
tone: Plain and direct
targetLength: 800
bannedPhrases: [game-changer]
---

Say what the scene shows, and let the silences do the rest.

Steps:
1. Give each character lines in the exchange, in the order the scene needs.
2. Give each speaker distinct diction: their own word choice, sentence length and forms of address, as their voice notes say.
3. Keep each speaker to the relationship notes: how they speak to each other character.
4. Carry the subtext under the lines, so that what the characters do not say shows.

Constraints:
- Use only the material above.
- Cite each factual sentence with its entity or source ID in the form [@id].
- Where a needed fact is missing, write TK with a short note in brackets, for example TK (the year the light was built). Do not invent it.
- Follow the tone of the style profile, avoid its banned phrases, and keep to the length above.
